replies.author: EdgarDruin
replies.body: I’ve been working on a top down 2D space sim.  I had a functional gate jump animation and tractor beams that move the ship through the gate gantry.  I asked it to improve them, saying the gate animation should be more like an implosion gate activation from stargate and the faint ray based beams more like soft transparent tractor beams.  Very basic instruction and it significantly improved both.  It was still working when I left, but it had fired up the test environment a few times already and I saw the working changes.  Looked much improved.

cmon AI industry, when are you gonna solve animation bruh... i've been waiting for so long 😭

replies.author: EtadanikM
replies.body: AI being great at animation requires training on actual animation rigging. Not much training data there. If there was a way to do continuous learning this would be a solved problem for it to just keep practicing until it gets it, but as it is all it can do is build better context.

replies.author: JohnJamesGutib
replies.body:
it sucks that gamedev seems to be especially affected by the jagged nature of ai intelligence due to how deeply multidisciplinary the field just is

the fact that we've gotten as far as we have in terms of ai gamedev is a small miracle, but it still bites hard in this specific case

replies.author: EtadanikM
replies.body:
Making games *is* hard. It's often called one of the hardest things you can do with computers. So honestly, it's not surprising it's the last frontier. 

But on the other hand, because Anthropic is almost certainly not training their models directly for game development, it's also a decent bench mark for general intelligence. If a model that isn't trained specifically for game development becomes comprehensively great at game development, I'd think AGI is pretty close.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/r4azrcq5vo0i1.png

:- / bit the bullet and filling up that utilization , aight it's wild , above is my character maker done in O5.5 max for a cyberpunk game i struggled alot with the necks and side views but F5.2 on max made the customizer polished .

Generally start with high to get the ground work then move to max in O5.5 to push , for F5.2 went max in browser then max in claude code. 

did the head and neck shapes , then the face elements , adding some more elements , then will do the torso -> arms -> , legs -> hair > then a facial rigging system followed by a movement rigging system . This will be my standard for characters in games @ 84% now should be able to get the entire thing in a week . 

I broke it down this way allowing claude to focus on the details i need.But yeah this shit it cooking, we have a few days at top tier until it's "collaborated / post release tuning" will also experiment with it as a orchestrator on opus , gpt and glm flash

comments.author: Reklaw12
comments.body:
It's a solid step up over opus 5.5 for modelling and animation. Expensive for now of course but if you're using a subscription (and you should for hobby gamedev, api prices are crazy!) it's worth a play with.

I have this little project [https://github.com/Joe975/mesh-jig](https://github.com/Joe975/mesh-jig) that lets coding agents or API llms build meshes with Blender then rig & animate them. You can see some examples [here](https://joe975.github.io/mesh-jig/?subject=horror&model=fable-5-2-high-api-agent-10-nov&clip=sprint&vs=opus-5-5#horror) \- fable vs opus 5.5 isn’t huge but it's still that much closer to game ready

https://i.redd.it/e9tipdzq2p0i1.gif
